title: Understanding Investment Funds for Policymakers
summary: An eight-module programme giving policymakers a clear grounding in how investment funds work, how they are regulated and the policy choices they raise.
intro: This training programme equips officials who shape funds policy with a clear understanding of how investment funds work, how they are regulated, where the risks lie and what drives a competitive, well-governed funds sector.

sections.Aim and Purpose: To give officials in finance ministries, central bank policy units and other public bodies a practical, non-technical grounding in investment funds, their role in the economy and the policy choices they raise. Participants leave able to understand industry and regulatory proposals, weigh investor protection and financial stability against growth and competitiveness, and contribute with confidence to funds policy and strategy.
sections.What It Covers: The purpose of investment funds and their place in the financial system, fund types, structures and strategies, parties and operations, how funds are regulated and supervised, liquidity, redemptions and fund suspensions, leverage and financial stability, taxation and the economics of a funds centre, and evaluating funds sector strategy and emerging issues.
Intended Audience: Officials in finance ministries and treasuries responsible for financial services and capital markets policy
Policy and financial stability staff in central banks and other public bodies who work on asset management
Advisers to ministers, parliamentary committees and economic development agencies dealing with the funds sector
Learning Objectives: Explain what investment funds are, why investors use them and their role in the economy
Distinguish the main fund types, legal structures and investment strategies
Describe how funds operate and the roles of the manager, depositary, administrator and other parties
Explain how funds are regulated and supervised and how this differs from the role of policymakers
Assess liquidity, leverage and financial stability risks, drawing on fund suspension case studies
Evaluate the tax, competitiveness and policy factors that shape a funds sector strategy
sections.Structure and Format: Eight modules of about three hours each, delivered in person, virtually or in a hybrid format, either as an intensive programme over two to three days or as a series of half-day sessions. Each module combines a plain-language briefing with case studies, explainers and policy discussion, and modules can be selected or tailored to the department's policy priorities.
sections.Useful Prior Knowledge and Experience: Some familiarity with financial services policy is helpful. No technical background in investment or fund management is required.
Core Reading: IOSCO, Objectives and Principles of Securities Regulation (2017)
FSB, Revised Policy Recommendations to Address Structural Vulnerabilities from Liquidity Mismatch in Open-Ended Funds (2023)
IOSCO, Recommendations for Liquidity Risk Management for Collective Investment Schemes (2018)
FSB, Global Monitoring Report on Non-Bank Financial Intermediation (annual)

modules.title: Investment Funds and Their Place in the Financial System
modules.summary: What an investment fund is, why savers and institutions use funds, and how the size and shape of the global funds industry has changed since the global financial crisis.
objectives: Explain how a fund pools money and how it differs from savings and other investment products
Describe who invests in funds and why
Summarise the size, growth and cross-border nature of the funds industry
syllabus: Saving versus investing and the basics of shares, bonds and derivatives
What a fund is and how investors buy and redeem units
Investor base: households, pension schemes, insurers and institutions
Industry size, growth, domiciles and cross-border distribution

modules.title: Fund Types, Structures and Strategies
modules.summary: The main families of fund and the legal forms they take, from retail and exchange-traded funds to hedge, private equity, real estate and money market funds.
objectives: Distinguish retail and professional-investor funds, open-ended and closed-ended
Describe common legal forms and structures, including umbrella and master-feeder funds
Explain the main investment strategies and emerging asset class trends
syllabus: Retail and professional-investor fund product rules
Legal forms: companies, unit trusts, contractual funds and partnerships
Umbrella funds, share classes, master-feeder and fund of funds
Exchange-traded, money market, hedge, private equity, real estate and private credit funds

modules.title: How Funds Work: Parties, Operations and Valuation
modules.summary: The fund value chain in practice: who manages, safeguards and administers a fund, how assets are valued and units priced, and how delegation and service providers create jobs and risks.
objectives: Describe the roles of the fund manager, depositary, administrator and other parties
Explain how net asset value is calculated and units are priced
Identify where delegation and outsourcing create operational and oversight risk
syllabus: Fund governance: boards, management companies and investment managers
Depositaries, custody, administration and transfer agency
Valuation, net asset value and fees
Delegation, outsourcing and substance requirements

modules.title: How Funds Are Regulated and Supervised
modules.summary: The building blocks of fund regulation, the international standards behind them, and how the responsibilities of policymakers, legislators and the supervisory authority fit together.
objectives: Explain the objectives of fund regulation: investor protection, market integrity and stability
Describe fund manager and fund product rules and the international standards that shape them
Distinguish the roles of policymakers and supervisors and how they work together
syllabus: IOSCO principles and the FSB's work on asset management
Fund manager authorisation and fund product rules
Disclosure, distribution and cross-border marketing of funds
Policymaker, legislator and supervisor: roles and coordination

modules.title: Liquidity, Redemptions and Fund Suspensions
modules.summary: Why liquidity mismatch matters, the tools funds use to manage redemptions, and what fund suspensions during market stress reveal about investor protection and wider stability.
objectives: Explain liquidity mismatch in open-ended funds and why it matters
Describe liquidity management tools and when they are used
Draw policy lessons from case studies of fund suspensions
syllabus: Liquidity mismatch, first-mover advantage and fire sales
Liquidity management tools: swing pricing, anti-dilution levies, gates and suspensions
Case studies: property and other fund suspensions in market stress
International policy responses and the questions they leave for policymakers

modules.title: Leverage, Interconnectedness and Financial Stability
modules.summary: What leverage means for an investment fund, how it is measured and disclosed, and why authorities see leverage, liquidity and interconnectedness in funds as a financial stability issue.
objectives: Distinguish cash and synthetic leverage and give examples of each
Explain the main leverage measurement methods and their limitations
Assess financial stability concerns and the macroprudential tools available
syllabus: Borrowing, securities lending, repos and derivatives as sources of leverage
Gross, commitment and value-at-risk methods
Disclosure of leverage to authorities and investors
Non-bank financial intermediation, money market funds and macroprudential limits

modules.title: Taxation, Competitiveness and the Economics of a Funds Centre
modules.summary: How tax treatment, legal infrastructure and the regulatory environment shape where funds are domiciled and serviced, and the economic value a funds sector brings.
objectives: Explain tax neutrality and the main tax issues for funds and their investors
Identify the factors that make a jurisdiction attractive for funds and fund services
Assess the economic contribution and risks of a funds sector
syllabus: Tax neutrality, withholding tax and investor-level taxation
Indirect tax on fund services and the role of tax treaties
Competitiveness factors: legal structures, regulation, talent and infrastructure
Employment, service exports and reputational and concentration risks

modules.title: Shaping Funds Policy: Strategy Reviews and Emerging Issues
modules.summary: Brings the programme together by examining how a funds sector strategy is reviewed, how policy options are weighed, and which emerging issues policymakers should prepare for.
objectives: Evaluate an industry strategy review and its evidence base
Weigh policy options against investor protection, stability and growth objectives
Anticipate emerging issues in private markets, sustainability and technology
syllabus: Anatomy of a funds sector strategy review: evidence, consultation and targets
Assessing policy proposals from industry and other stakeholders
Emerging issues: private markets, sustainable funds, tokenisation and AI
Workshop: reviewing a funds sector strategy and agreeing policy priorities

related.title: Building a Competitive Financial Centre: Strategy, Regulation and Investment Promotion
related.summary: An eight-module programme helping ministries and investment promotion agencies build a competitive, reputable financial centre and measure the results.

related.title: Developing Capital Markets and Investment Fund Industries
related.summary: An eight-module programme helping policymakers develop deep, well-regulated capital markets and fund industries through credible, well-sequenced reform.

related.title: AI in Financial Services: Policy Choices for Government
related.summary: An eight-module programme helping policymakers understand AI in financial services and make informed choices on regulation, institutional roles and national strategy.

related.title: Digital Assets and Blockchain: A Policy Programme for Government
related.summary: An eight-module programme giving policymakers the understanding to set digital asset policy, design legislation and meet international standards on crypto-assets and stablecoins.

related.title: Drafting Financial Services Legislation
related.summary: An eight-module programme helping legislative drafters and legal advisers design and draft effective, enforceable and technology-neutral financial services legislation.

related.title: Financial Crises and Public Finances: Crisis Preparedness for Government
related.summary: An eight-module advanced programme preparing finance ministries and senior officials to manage financial crises, protect public finances and coordinate resolution.
